VIDEO.title: Matthew 13:44-58 – The Treasure Hidden In Jesus' Parables
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

hand: Every scribe who has become a disciple brings out of his treasure things new and old.
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Matthew 13:44-58. Jesus finishes His parables with the treasure hidden in a field, the pearl of great value, the dragnet, and the head of a household who brings out things new and old. Then He goes to His hometown, where they take offense at the carpenter's son, and He does not do many miracles there because of their unbelief.

The treasure and the pearl are a pair, like the mustard seed and the leaven, within the larger chiasm of 13:3-52. People expected the kingdom to explode onto the scene; Jesus says it is hidden, like treasure that must be searched for. That should have made His hearers lean in and look for a remez.

Hidden things run through the chapter: 'things hidden since the foundation of the world' (13:35) and the mysteries given to the disciples (13:11). The hidden treasure also sends the hearer back to Proverbs 2, already linked to the good soil: 'search for her as for hidden treasures… then you will understand' (Proverbs 2:4-5).

The dragnet has two hints. Ezekiel 47 pictures water flowing from a new temple, making the Dead Sea fresh, with fishermen spreading nets 'from Engedi to Eneglaim': a new Eden at the end of the age. And 'weeping and gnashing of teeth' points again to Psalm 35:16.

The chapter's question is 'Have you understood all these things?' (13:51). The scribe trained for the kingdom is the disciple; the treasure, the video argues, is God's word; and with Craig Blomberg, the old is the Hebrew Scriptures and the new is their fulfillment in the kingdom age. The lesson: the disciples of Jesus should love God's word so much that it shapes who they are, how they think, and what they do for His kingdom.
QUOTES: They were looking for the explosion.
Have you understood all these things?
The disciples of Jesus should love God's word so much that it will shape who they are, how they think, and what they do for his kingdom.
Everything is connected to God's word meaningfully.

LSB_QUOTES.text: “Have you understood all these things?” They *said to Him, “Yes.”
Therefore every scribe who has become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven is like a head of a household, who brings out of his treasure things new and old.
If you seek her as silver / And search for her as for hidden treasures;

src.text: “The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid again; and from joy over it he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field. “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking fine pearls, and upon finding one pearl of great value, he went and sold all that he had and bought it.

lines.text: Two small stories meant to be heard together, like the mustard seed and the leaven earlier (13:31-33). Both pairs mirror each other within the chiasm of 13:3-52.
In both, a man finds something of surpassing worth and sells all he has, the first 'from joy over it.'

How did people expect the kingdom to arrive? The video thinks they were looking for the explosion, more like John the Baptist's picture of the axe and the fire. Parables about something hidden that must be searched for should have sounded odd.
So the hearers should have leaned in and looked for a remez, a hint back to the Old Testament, if they were truly seeking understanding.

TREASURE.title: Things hidden since the foundation of the world

left.text: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, / “I will open My mouth in parables; / I will utter things hidden since the foundation of the world.”

right.text: And Jesus answered and said to them, “To you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given.

lines.text: At the center of the chiasm Jesus says He is uttering hidden things, and earlier He told the disciples the mysteries are given to them, not to the crowds. Notice the pattern of hiddenness.

TREASURE.title: Search for her as for hidden treasures

src.text: For if you call out for understanding, / Give your voice for discernment; / If you seek her as silver / And search for her as for hidden treasures; / Then you will understand the fear of Yahweh / And find the knowledge of God.

lines.text: Jesus had already tied Proverbs 2 to the good soil, the one who 'hears the word and understands it' (13:23). Notice how often Proverbs 2 says 'understand.' Jesus retreads the same link to make a slightly different point.

src.text: “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet cast into the sea, and gathering fish of every kind; and when it was filled, they drew it up on the beach; and they sat down and gathered the good fish into containers, but the bad they threw away. So it will be at the end of the age; the angels will come forth and take out the wicked from among the righteous, and will throw them into the fiery furnace; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

lines.text: Jesus ties this picture to the end of the age. Is there an Old Testament passage about fishermen spreading nets that is also about the end times? Yes: Ezekiel 47.

src.text: Then he said to me, “These waters go out toward the eastern region and go down into the Arabah; then they go toward the sea, being made to flow out to the sea, and the waters of the sea will be healed. And it will be that every living creature, which swarms in every place where the river goes, will live. And there will be very many fish, for these waters go there and the other waters are healed; so everything will live where the river goes. And it will be that fishermen will stand beside it; from Engedi to Eneglaim there will be a place for the spreading of nets. Their fish will be according to their kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many.

lines.text: Water flows from a new temple, and wherever it goes everything lives. Fishermen stand beside the sea and spread their nets for fish of very many kinds, like the dragnet's 'fish of every kind.'
It is a new Eden: trees whose leaves do not wither, fruit for food and leaves for healing (Ezekiel 47:12). This is entirely eschatological, a promise for the whole world.
The 'sea' here is the Dead Sea: the river goes down into the Arabah, and Engedi lies on its western shore. Revelation 22:1-2 takes up the same picture.

src.text: Now on the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink. He who believes in Me, as the Scripture said, ‘From his innermost being will flow rivers of living water.’”

lines.text: As an aside, the video says that at the feast Jesus announces that He is the true source of the water that flows from the new temple.
John adds, 'But this He spoke of the Spirit' (John 7:39). At the Feast of Booths a priest poured water from the Siloam pool at the altar (Mishnah Sukkah 4:9).

left.text: and will throw them into the fiery furnace; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

right.text: Amongst the godless jesters at a feast, / They gnashed at me with their teeth.

lines.text: The second hint repeats 13:42 word for word. The video links it again to Psalm 35, where David asks the Lord to save him from the wicked who surround him to do him harm.

SCRIBE.title: Have you understood all these things?

src.text: “Have you understood all these things?” They *said to Him, “Yes.” And He said to them, “Therefore every scribe who has become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven is like a head of a household, who brings out of his treasure things new and old.”

lines.text: The whole discourse leads to this question, and the question extends to us. This short, pithy parable puts the bow on top of the chiasm.
Who is the scribe trained for the kingdom? Clearly the disciples, whom Jesus has been training since the Sermon on the Mount.

The treasure could be the kingdom itself, brought out for the world to see; some argue for this. The video leans toward God's word, because the hidden treasure in Proverbs 2 is God's commandments: 'treasure my commandments within you' (Proverbs 2:1).
With Craig Blomberg: as the disciples teach God's will, they draw out the meaning of the Hebrew Scriptures (the old) while showing how they are fulfilled and applied in the kingdom age (the new).

left.text: A student is not above his teacher; but everyone, after he has been fully trained, will be like his teacher.

right.text: All Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for training in righteousness,

lines.text: The disciples of Jesus should love God's word so much that it shapes who they are, how they think, and what they do for His kingdom. More is required than knowing and relaying what Jesus said: they must give up their own expectations and become like their teacher by the power of the Holy Spirit.
Then they will recognize that everything happening around them is connected to God's word. They bring out something new, their obedience, from something old, God's word.

SCRIBE.title: Is not this the carpenter's son?

src.text: Is not this the carpenter’s son? Is not His mother called Mary, and His brothers, James and Joseph and Simon and Judas? And His sisters, are they not all with us? Where then did this man get all these things?” And they were taking offense at Him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and in his own household.” And He did not do many miracles there because of their unbelief.

lines.text: They take offense not because He did something wrong but because He challenged their expectations. It is a recurring theme: not only corrupt leaders but ordinary people from His own town.
Jesus has nothing to prove to those who will not let go of their expectations. As He refused the scribes and Pharisees a sign (12:39), He does not do mighty works for the people of Nazareth.

TERMS.def: Valuables buried for safekeeping, common in a land often invaded; a finder could buy the field.
In the ancient world one of the most precious goods, sought by merchants from the Red Sea and Persian Gulf.
A long net drawn through the water and hauled to shore, catching fish of every kind.
A hint that sends the hearer back to an Old Testament passage. The captions write 'Rome' and 'rese.'
The four levels of interpretation from the last episode; the captions write 'partz.'
A trained teacher of the Law; Jesus speaks of a scribe 'who has become a disciple' of the kingdom.
About the last things: here the end of the age and the new creation.
Greek tektōn: a builder or craftsman in wood or stone.

WORDS.gloss: Treasure; also a storeroom or treasure chest.
To make a disciple; passive, to become a disciple. Look up: BDAG, μαθητεύω.
Net (a homonym of the word for a thing devoted to God). Look up: BDB or HALOT, חֵרֶם II.

BACKGROUND.p: With no banks and frequent wars, people buried coins and valuables in the ground. The Copper Scroll from Qumran is a list of hidden treasures. A man who found treasure in another's field could buy the field to own it lawfully.

On the Sea of Galilee a dragnet was spread from a boat and hauled to the beach by teams on shore. The catch was sorted: unclean fish without fins and scales (Leviticus 11:9-12) and worthless ones were thrown away.

BACKGROUND.h: Water at the Feast of Booths
BACKGROUND.p: At the Feast of Booths a golden jug was filled at the pool of Siloam and the water poured at the altar. The Mishnah says, 'One who did not see the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing of the Water never saw celebration in his days' (Mishnah Sukkah 5:1).
Nazareth was a small village in the hills of lower Galilee, a few kilometers from the rebuilt city of Sepphoris. A builder there could have found work in the region.

WITNESSES.text: Much as in the other place, the mustard seed and the leaven have but some little difference from each other, so here also these two parables, that of the treasure and that of the pearl.
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Matthew 47, on 13:44-46. Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 10 (public domain).

WITNESSES.text: Do you see how so far from excluding the Old Testament, He even commends it, and speaks publicly in favor of it, calling it a treasure?
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Matthew 47, on 13:52. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

WITNESSES.text: while He slackens somewhat in His miracles; so as not to inflame them unto more envy, nor to condemn them more grievously, by the aggravation of their unbelief
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Matthew 48, on 13:58. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

DEBATES.p: Most read the man and the merchant as anyone who discovers the kingdom and gives up everything for it. Others read the buyer as Christ, who gave all to purchase His people (compare 1 Corinthians 6:20).

DEBATES.h: What are the things 'new and old'?
DEBATES.p: The video, with Blomberg and Chrysostom, reads the old as the Hebrew Scriptures and the new as their fulfillment in Jesus. Others read new and old as Jesus' teaching alongside the Law, or simply the whole range of a disciple's learning.
Some read the rivers as flowing from the believer, others from Christ Himself, the new temple. John's note that 'this He spoke of the Spirit' (John 7:39) fits both readings.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: The video says Jesus 'refuses to perform mighty works' in Nazareth. Matthew says 'He did not do many miracles there because of their unbelief' (13:58), and Mark adds that He 'laid His hands on a few sick people and healed them' (Mark 6:5).
The center of the chiasm is given as verses 34-43 here and 37-43 in the last episode; the outline is the video's own, and scholars arrange the chapter in several ways.

Reading John 7:37-38 as Jesus announcing that He is the source of Ezekiel's temple river is an interpretation; the text says the rivers flow 'from his innermost being,' and John explains it of the Spirit (7:39).
Craig Blomberg's view is given as the video reports it; we could not check it against his book.
The captions write 'Engeti to Enagim' for Engedi to Eneglaim, 'partz' for PaRDeS, 'Rome' and 'rese' for remez, and 'Blumbberg' for Blomberg.

QUESTIONS: What would you 'sell' for the kingdom? Is there anything you are holding back?
Can you state the point of Matthew 13:3-52 in two sentences?
Why do you think the kingdom came hidden rather than explosive?
Which 'old' passage of Scripture has become 'new' to you because of Jesus?
Where might familiarity with Jesus be making you less open to Him, like the people of Nazareth?
Is God's word shaping who you are, how you think, and what you do? Where do you see it, and where not yet?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The lesson for the original audience: the disciples of Jesus should love God's word so much that it will shape who they are, how they think, and what they do for His kingdom. A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone fully trained will be like his teacher (Luke 6:40). More is required than knowing what Jesus said and relaying it to someone else: the disciples must give up everything, including their own expectations, and humble themselves to become like their teacher, embodying His qualities by the power of the Holy Spirit and living out His teaching as much as they speak it. If they understand and obey, they will recognize that everything happening around them is connected to God's word. As Paul told Timothy, all Scripture is God-breathed and equips the man of God for every good work. If they do this, they will bring out something new, the expression of their obedience to the Lord, from something old, God's word. Do God's people love God's word so much that they seek to be completely shaped by it today? Does this describe you?

## The dragnet and Ezekiel's river
1. Matthew 13:47-50: The dragnet
   End of the age Matthew 13:47-50: "“Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet cast into the sea, and gathering fish of every kind; and when it was filled, they drew it up on the beach; and they sat down and gathered the good fish into containers, but the bad they threw away. So it will be at the end of the age; the angels will come forth and take out the wicked from among the righteous, and will throw them into the fiery furnace; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+13:47-50
   (video) Jesus ties this picture to the end of the age. Is there an Old Testament passage about fishermen spreading nets that is also about the end times? Yes: Ezekiel 47.
2. Ezekiel 47:1-12: A river from the temple
   New Eden Ezekiel 47:8-10: "Then he said to me, “These waters go out toward the eastern region and go down into the Arabah; then they go toward the sea, being made to flow out to the sea, and the waters of the sea will be healed. And it will be that every living creature, which swarms in every place where the river goes, will live. And there will be very many fish, for these waters go there and the other waters are healed; so everything will live where the river goes. And it will be that fishermen will stand beside it; from Engedi to Eneglaim there will be a place for the spreading of nets. Their fish will be according to their kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Ezekiel+47:8-10
   (video) Water flows from a new temple, and wherever it goes everything lives. Fishermen stand beside the sea and spread their nets for fish of very many kinds, like the dragnet's 'fish of every kind.'
   (video) It is a new Eden: trees whose leaves do not wither, fruit for food and leaves for healing (Ezekiel 47:12). This is entirely eschatological, a promise for the whole world. (Ezekiel 47:12)
   [Background] The 'sea' here is the Dead Sea: the river goes down into the Arabah, and Engedi lies on its western shore. Revelation 22:1-2 takes up the same picture. (Revelation 22:1-2)
3. John 7:37-39: Rivers of living water
   Aside John 7:37-38: "Now on the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink. He who believes in Me, as the Scripture said, ‘From his innermost being will flow rivers of living water.’”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=John+7:37-38
   (video) As an aside, the video says that at the feast Jesus announces that He is the true source of the water that flows from the new temple.
   [Background] John adds, 'But this He spoke of the Spirit' (John 7:39). At the Feast of Booths a priest poured water from the Siloam pool at the altar (Mishnah Sukkah 4:9). (John 7:39)
4. Matthew 13:42, 50: Weeping and gnashing again
   Jesus (Matthew 13:50, LSB): "and will throw them into the fiery furnace; in that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."
   David (Psalms 35:16, LSB): "Amongst the godless jesters at a feast, / They gnashed at me with their teeth."
   (video) The second hint repeats 13:42 word for word. The video links it again to Psalm 35, where David asks the Lord to save him from the wicked who surround him to do him harm.

## Things new and old
1. Matthew 13:51-52: Have you understood all these things?
   The point Matthew 13:51-52: "“Have you understood all these things?” They *said to Him, “Yes.” And He said to them, “Therefore every scribe who has become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven is like a head of a household, who brings out of his treasure things new and old.”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+13:51-52
   (video) The whole discourse leads to this question, and the question extends to us. This short, pithy parable puts the bow on top of the chiasm.
   (video) Who is the scribe trained for the kingdom? Clearly the disciples, whom Jesus has been training since the Sermon on the Mount.
2. What is the treasure?: The kingdom, or God's word?
   (video) The treasure could be the kingdom itself, brought out for the world to see; some argue for this. The video leans toward God's word, because the hidden treasure in Proverbs 2 is God's commandments: 'treasure my commandments within you' (Proverbs 2:1). (Proverbs 2:1)
   (video) With Craig Blomberg: as the disciples teach God's will, they draw out the meaning of the Hebrew Scriptures (the old) while showing how they are fulfilled and applied in the kingdom age (the new).
3. Luke 6:40; 2 Timothy 3:16-17: Shaped by the word
   Jesus (Luke 6:40, LSB): "A student is not above his teacher; but everyone, after he has been fully trained, will be like his teacher."
   Paul (2 Timothy 3:16, LSB): "All Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for training in righteousness,"
   (video) The disciples of Jesus should love God's word so much that it shapes who they are, how they think, and what they do for His kingdom. More is required than knowing and relaying what Jesus said: they must give up their own expectations and become like their teacher by the power of the Holy Spirit.
   (video) Then they will recognize that everything happening around them is connected to God's word. They bring out something new, their obedience, from something old, God's word.
4. Matthew 13:53-58: Is not this the carpenter's son?
   Nazareth Matthew 13:55-58: "Is not this the carpenter’s son? Is not His mother called Mary, and His brothers, James and Joseph and Simon and Judas? And His sisters, are they not all with us? Where then did this man get all these things?” And they were taking offense at Him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and in his own household.” And He did not do many miracles there because of their unbelief." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+13:55-58
   (video) They take offense not because He did something wrong but because He challenged their expectations. It is a recurring theme: not only corrupt leaders but ordinary people from His own town.
   (video) Jesus has nothing to prove to those who will not let go of their expectations. As He refused the scribes and Pharisees a sign (12:39), He does not do mighty works for the people of Nazareth. (Matthew 12:39)

## Key people
- Jesus: Finishes the parables and asks, 'Have you understood all these things?' [Background] In Nazareth He is known as 'the carpenter's son' (13:55); Mark has 'the carpenter' (Mark 6:3).
- The disciples: The scribes trained for the kingdom, who must bring out things new and old. [Background] They answer 'Yes' (13:51), though they will still struggle to understand (15:16; 16:9).
- The man and the merchant: Each finds something of surpassing worth and sells all he has. [Background] Compare the rich young man, who went away grieving (19:21-22).
- Ezekiel: Saw water flow from a new temple and fishermen spreading nets by the sea. [Background] A priest among the exiles in Babylon (Ezekiel 1:1-3).
- The people of Nazareth: Refuse to see Him as more than a carpenter's son; they take offense. [Background] Luke tells of an earlier visit when they tried to throw Him off a cliff (Luke 4:28-30).
- Mary and His brothers: Named by the townspeople: James, Joseph, Simon and Judas. [Background] James later led the church in Jerusalem (Acts 15:13), and Judas is usually linked with the letter of Jude.

## Places [Background]
- Nazareth (named in the video): Jesus' hometown, where they took offense at the carpenter's son (13:54-57).
- Capernaum: Where Jesus taught the parables by the sea and in the house (13:1, 36).
- Jerusalem: The temple city: in Ezekiel's vision the river flows east from the temple (Ezekiel 47:1).
- Eneglaim (proposed) (named in the video): One end of Ezekiel's fishing shore (47:10); often placed at Ein Feshkha on the north-west shore of the Dead Sea. The site is uncertain.

## Key terms
- Hidden treasure: Valuables buried for safekeeping, common in a land often invaded; a finder could buy the field.
- Pearl: In the ancient world one of the most precious goods, sought by merchants from the Red Sea and Persian Gulf.
- Dragnet: A long net drawn through the water and hauled to shore, catching fish of every kind.
- Remez: A hint that sends the hearer back to an Old Testament passage. The captions write 'Rome' and 'rese.'
- PaRDeS: The four levels of interpretation from the last episode; the captions write 'partz.'
- Scribe: A trained teacher of the Law; Jesus speaks of a scribe 'who has become a disciple' of the kingdom.
- Eschatological: About the last things: here the end of the age and the new creation.
- Carpenter: Greek tektōn: a builder or craftsman in wood or stone. [Background]

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Buried treasure: With no banks and frequent wars, people buried coins and valuables in the ground. The Copper Scroll from Qumran is a list of hidden treasures. A man who found treasure in another's field could buy the field to own it lawfully.
- Fishing with a dragnet: On the Sea of Galilee a dragnet was spread from a boat and hauled to the beach by teams on shore. The catch was sorted: unclean fish without fins and scales (Leviticus 11:9-12) and worthless ones were thrown away.
- Water at the Feast of Booths: At the Feast of Booths a golden jug was filled at the pool of Siloam and the water poured at the altar. The Mishnah says, 'One who did not see the Celebration of the Place of the Drawing of the Water never saw celebration in his days' (Mishnah Sukkah 5:1).
- Nazareth: Nazareth was a small village in the hills of lower Galilee, a few kilometers from the rebuilt city of Sepphoris. A builder there could have found work in the region.

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Who finds the treasure? Most read the man and the merchant as anyone who discovers the kingdom and gives up everything for it. Others read the buyer as Christ, who gave all to purchase His people (compare 1 Corinthians 6:20).
- What are the things 'new and old'? The video, with Blomberg and Chrysostom, reads the old as the Hebrew Scriptures and the new as their fulfillment in Jesus. Others read new and old as Jesus' teaching alongside the Law, or simply the whole range of a disciple's learning.
- Whose 'innermost being' in John 7:38? Some read the rivers as flowing from the believer, others from Christ Himself, the new temple. John's note that 'this He spoke of the Spirit' (John 7:39) fits both readings.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- The video says Jesus 'refuses to perform mighty works' in Nazareth. Matthew says 'He did not do many miracles there because of their unbelief' (13:58), and Mark adds that He 'laid His hands on a few sick people and healed them' (Mark 6:5).
- The center of the chiasm is given as verses 34-43 here and 37-43 in the last episode; the outline is the video's own, and scholars arrange the chapter in several ways.
- Reading John 7:37-38 as Jesus announcing that He is the source of Ezekiel's temple river is an interpretation; the text says the rivers flow 'from his innermost being,' and John explains it of the Spirit (7:39).
- Craig Blomberg's view is given as the video reports it; we could not check it against his book.
- The captions write 'Engeti to Enagim' for Engedi to Eneglaim, 'partz' for PaRDeS, 'Rome' and 'rese' for remez, and 'Blumbberg' for Blomberg.

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. What would you 'sell' for the kingdom? Is there anything you are holding back?
2. Can you state the point of Matthew 13:3-52 in two sentences?
3. Why do you think the kingdom came hidden rather than explosive?
4. Which 'old' passage of Scripture has become 'new' to you because of Jesus?
5. Where might familiarity with Jesus be making you less open to Him, like the people of Nazareth?
6. Is God's word shaping who you are, how you think, and what you do? Where do you see it, and where not yet?

## Application
- (video) The lesson for the original audience: the disciples of Jesus should love God's word so much that it will shape who they are, how they think, and what they do for His kingdom. A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone fully trained will be like his teacher (Luke 6:40). More is required than knowing what Jesus said and relaying it to someone else: the disciples must give up everything, including their own expectations, and humble themselves to become like their teacher, embodying His qualities by the power of the Holy Spirit and living out His teaching as much as they speak it. If they understand and obey, they will recognize that everything happening around them is connected to God's word. As Paul told Timothy, all Scripture is God-breathed and equips the man of God for every good work. If they do this, they will bring out something new, the expression of their obedience to the Lord, from something old, God's word. Do God's people love God's word so much that they seek to be completely shaped by it today? Does this describe you?
- Study note (added): try the teacher's exercise. Write the point of Matthew 13:3-52 in two sentences, then read Proverbs 2:1-10 and underline every word for seeking and understanding.
